note: Starter set of major events, hand-written for v0.1. Each entry links to its Wikipedia article as the source. 'approx' marks dates that are approximate, traditional or disputed. Needs review before being treated as authoritative.

events.title: Neolithic Revolution begins
events.summary: Communities in the Fertile Crescent begin farming and settling permanently, one of the most important transitions in human history.

events.title: Writing emerges in Sumer
events.summary: Cuneiform script develops in Mesopotamian cities such as Uruk, among the earliest known writing systems.

events.title: Unification of Egypt
events.summary: Upper and Lower Egypt are united under one king, traditionally Narmer, opening the Early Dynastic Period.

events.title: Great Pyramid of Giza built
events.summary: Built for the pharaoh Khufu, it remained the tallest human-made structure for over 3,800 years.

events.title: Sargon founds the Akkadian Empire
events.summary: Often described as the first empire, uniting the city-states of Mesopotamia under a single ruler.

events.title: Code of Hammurabi
events.summary: The Babylonian king Hammurabi issues one of the most complete surviving early law codes.

events.title: Battle of Kadesh
events.summary: Egypt under Ramesses II fights the Hittite Empire; it led to one of the earliest known peace treaties.

events.title: First recorded Olympic Games
events.summary: The traditional date of the first Olympic Games at Olympia, later used by Greeks to count years.

events.title: Legendary founding of Rome
events.summary: The traditional date for Romulus founding Rome. Archaeology shows the settlement is older; the date is legendary.

events.title: Cyrus the Great founds the Achaemenid Empire
events.summary: Cyrus overthrows the Medes and builds what becomes the largest empire the world had yet seen.

events.title: Battle of Marathon
events.summary: Athens and Plataea defeat the first Persian invasion of Greece.

events.title: Peloponnesian War
events.summary: Athens and its empire fight Sparta and its allies; Sparta wins, ending Athenian dominance in Greece.

events.title: Conquests of Alexander the Great
events.summary: Alexander of Macedon conquers the Persian Empire and reaches India, spreading Greek culture across the region.

events.title: Maurya Empire founded
events.summary: Chandragupta Maurya founds an empire that comes to cover most of the Indian subcontinent.

events.title: Punic Wars
events.summary: Three wars between Rome and Carthage end with Carthage destroyed and Rome dominant in the western Mediterranean.

events.title: Qin unifies China
events.summary: Qin Shi Huang conquers the rival Warring States and becomes the first emperor of a unified China.

events.title: Han dynasty founded
events.summary: Liu Bang founds the Han dynasty, which rules China for about four centuries.

events.title: Assassination of Julius Caesar
events.summary: Senators kill Caesar on the Ides of March, setting off the civil wars that end the Roman Republic.

events.title: Augustus becomes first Roman emperor
events.summary: Octavian receives the title Augustus; this is conventionally treated as the start of the Roman Empire.

events.title: Battle of the Teutoburg Forest
events.summary: Germanic tribes under Arminius destroy three Roman legions, halting Roman expansion east of the Rhine.

events.title: End of the Han dynasty
events.summary: The last Han emperor abdicates and China splits into the Three Kingdoms of Wei, Shu and Wu.

events.title: Edict of Milan
events.summary: Constantine and Licinius grant religious tolerance across the Roman Empire, including to Christians.

events.title: Constantinople becomes the imperial capital
events.summary: Constantine dedicates his new capital on the site of Byzantium; it remains a capital for over 1,500 years.

events.title: Fall of the Western Roman Empire
events.summary: Odoacer deposes Romulus Augustulus, the last western emperor, a date often used to mark the end of antiquity.
events.wiki: Fall of the Western Roman Empire

events.title: The Hijra
events.summary: Muhammad and his followers migrate from Mecca to Medina; the year begins the Islamic calendar.

events.title: Early Muslim conquests
events.summary: Arab armies spread out from Arabia, conquering the Sasanian Empire and much of the Byzantine Empire, North Africa and Iberia.

events.title: Battle of Tours
events.summary: Frankish forces under Charles Martel defeat an Umayyad army in central France.

events.title: Founding of Baghdad
events.summary: The Abbasid caliph al-Mansur founds Baghdad, which becomes a centre of learning in the Islamic Golden Age.

events.title: Charlemagne crowned emperor
events.summary: Pope Leo III crowns Charlemagne Emperor of the Romans in Rome on Christmas Day.

events.title: Treaty of Verdun
events.summary: Charlemagne's grandsons split the Carolingian Empire into three kingdoms, foreshadowing France and Germany.

events.title: Song dynasty founded
events.summary: Zhao Kuangyin reunifies most of China; the Song era sees major advances in technology, commerce and printing.

events.title: East–West Schism
events.summary: Mutual excommunications split Christianity into the Catholic West and the Orthodox East.

events.title: Battle of Hastings
events.summary: William of Normandy defeats Harold II and begins the Norman conquest of England.

events.title: First Crusade
events.summary: European armies march to the Levant and capture Jerusalem, founding the Crusader states.

events.title: Genghis Khan founds the Mongol Empire
events.summary: Temüjin is proclaimed Genghis Khan; his empire becomes the largest contiguous land empire in history.

events.title: Magna Carta
events.summary: King John agrees to a charter limiting royal power, later seen as a foundation of constitutional law.

events.title: Mongol sack of Baghdad
events.summary: Mongol forces under Hulagu capture and sack Baghdad, ending the Abbasid Caliphate there.

events.title: Yuan dynasty proclaimed
events.summary: Kublai Khan proclaims the Yuan dynasty, ruling China from Khanbaliq (modern Beijing).

events.title: Battle of Yamen
events.summary: The Yuan navy destroys the last Song forces, completing the Mongol conquest of China.

events.title: Hundred Years' War
events.summary: A series of conflicts between England and France over the French throne; France ultimately prevails.

events.title: Black Death
events.summary: Plague kills an estimated 30–60% of Europe's population, with huge losses across Asia and North Africa too.

events.title: Ming dynasty founded
events.summary: Zhu Yuanzhang drives out the Yuan and founds the Ming dynasty, first ruling from Nanjing.

events.title: Fall of Constantinople
events.summary: The Ottoman Empire under Mehmed II captures Constantinople, ending the Byzantine Empire.

events.title: Columbus reaches the Americas
events.summary: Columbus lands in the Bahamas, beginning lasting contact between Europe and the Americas, with devastating results for Indigenous peoples.

events.title: Treaty of Tordesillas
events.summary: Spain and Portugal divide newly encountered lands outside Europe along a meridian in the Atlantic.

events.title: Luther's Ninety-five Theses
events.summary: Martin Luther's challenge to Church practices in Wittenberg sparks the Protestant Reformation.

events.title: Spanish conquest of the Aztec Empire
events.summary: Hernán Cortés and Indigenous allies overthrow the Aztec Empire and take Tenochtitlan.
events.wiki: Spanish conquest of the Aztec Empire

events.title: First Battle of Panipat
events.summary: Babur defeats the Delhi Sultanate and founds the Mughal Empire.

events.title: Spanish Armada
events.summary: A Spanish fleet sent to invade England is defeated and scattered.

events.title: Tokugawa shogunate established
events.summary: Tokugawa Ieyasu becomes shogun, beginning over 250 years of relative peace and isolation in Japan.

events.title: Thirty Years' War
events.summary: A war centred on the Holy Roman Empire, among the most destructive in European history.

events.title: Qing dynasty takes Beijing
events.summary: After the Ming collapse, the Manchu Qing dynasty enters Beijing and goes on to rule China until 1912.

events.title: Peace of Westphalia
events.summary: Treaties ending the Thirty Years' War, often cited as a foundation of the modern system of sovereign states.

events.title: Battle of Vienna
events.summary: A Habsburg–Polish force breaks the Ottoman siege of Vienna, a turning point in Ottoman expansion into Europe.

events.title: Glorious Revolution
events.summary: James II is replaced by William III and Mary II, followed by the Bill of Rights limiting royal power.

events.title: War of the Spanish Succession
events.summary: European powers fight over who inherits the Spanish throne; it reshapes the balance of power in Europe.

events.title: Peace of Utrecht
events.summary: Treaties that end most of the War of the Spanish Succession; Britain gains Gibraltar and Newfoundland.

events.title: Seven Years' War
events.summary: A conflict fought in Europe, the Americas and Asia; Britain emerges as the leading colonial power.

events.title: US Declaration of Independence
events.summary: Thirteen British colonies declare independence during the American Revolutionary War.

events.title: Treaty of Paris (1783)
events.summary: Britain recognises the independence of the United States, ending the American Revolutionary War.

events.title: French Revolution
events.summary: Revolution overthrows the French monarchy, spreading ideas of popular sovereignty and citizens' rights.

events.title: Napoleonic Wars
events.summary: Napoleon's France fights coalitions of European powers, redrawing the map of Europe.

events.title: Haitian independence
events.summary: After the only successful large-scale revolt by enslaved people, Haiti becomes the first independent nation in the Caribbean.

events.title: Spanish American wars of independence
events.summary: Spain's colonies across the Americas fight for and win their independence.

events.title: Congress of Vienna
events.summary: European powers redraw the continent's borders after Napoleon's defeat.

events.title: First Opium War
events.summary: Britain defeats Qing China; the Treaty of Nanking cedes Hong Kong and opens ports to foreign trade.

events.title: Revolutions of 1848
events.summary: A wave of revolutions sweeps Europe, demanding liberal reform and national self-rule.

events.title: Indian Rebellion of 1857
events.summary: A large uprising against East India Company rule leads Britain to rule India directly.

events.title: American Civil War
events.summary: The Union defeats the Confederacy, preserving the United States and ending slavery there.

events.title: Meiji Restoration
events.summary: Imperial rule is restored in Japan, beginning rapid modernisation and industrialisation.

events.title: Unification of Germany
events.summary: The German Empire is proclaimed at Versailles after Prussia defeats France.

events.title: Congress of Berlin
events.summary: European powers revise the map of the Balkans after the Russo-Turkish War.

events.title: Berlin Conference
events.summary: European powers set rules for colonising Africa, accelerating the 'Scramble for Africa'.

events.title: World War I
events.summary: Triggered by the assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand in Sarajevo; it destroys four empires and kills millions.

events.title: Russian Revolution
events.summary: The Tsar is overthrown and the Bolsheviks take power, leading to civil war and the Soviet state.

events.title: Treaty of Versailles
events.summary: The main peace treaty ending World War I imposes territorial losses and reparations on Germany.

events.title: Soviet Union founded
events.summary: Soviet Russia, Ukraine, Belarus and the Transcaucasian republic form the USSR.
events.wiki: Treaty on the Creation of the USSR

events.title: Republic of Turkey proclaimed
events.summary: Mustafa Kemal Atatürk proclaims the republic after the end of the Ottoman Empire.

events.title: Wall Street Crash
events.summary: The US stock market collapse helps trigger the Great Depression worldwide.

events.title: Munich Agreement
events.summary: Britain, France and Italy allow Nazi Germany to annex the Sudetenland from Czechoslovakia.

events.title: World War II
events.summary: The deadliest conflict in history, beginning with Germany's invasion of Poland and ending with Allied victory.

events.title: Atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki
events.summary: The United States drops two atomic bombs on Japan, the only use of nuclear weapons in war.
events.wiki: Atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki

events.title: United Nations founded
events.summary: The UN Charter is signed in San Francisco to maintain international peace and security.

events.title: Cold War
events.summary: Decades of rivalry between the United States and the Soviet Union and their allies, fought mostly through proxies.

events.title: Partition of India
events.summary: British India is divided into India and Pakistan, with mass migration and widespread violence.

events.title: Israeli Declaration of Independence
events.summary: Israel declares independence, followed immediately by the 1948 Arab–Israeli War and the Palestinian Nakba.

events.title: People's Republic of China proclaimed
events.summary: Mao Zedong proclaims the PRC after the Communists win the Chinese Civil War.
events.wiki: Proclamation of the People's Republic of China

events.title: Korean War
events.summary: North Korea, backed by China and the USSR, fights South Korea and UN forces; it ends in an armistice.

events.title: Vietnam War
events.summary: North Vietnam and its allies fight South Vietnam and the United States, ending with the fall of Saigon.

events.title: Year of Africa
events.summary: Seventeen African nations gain independence in a single year as decolonisation accelerates.

events.title: Cuban Missile Crisis
events.summary: A thirteen-day standoff over Soviet missiles in Cuba brings the world close to nuclear war.

events.title: Fall of the Berlin Wall
events.summary: East Germany opens its border, a defining moment in the collapse of communist rule in Eastern Europe.

events.title: Dissolution of the Soviet Union
events.summary: The USSR breaks into fifteen independent states, ending the Cold War.

events.title: Maastricht Treaty
events.summary: The treaty creating the European Union is signed.

events.title: End of apartheid in South Africa
events.summary: South Africa's first fully democratic election makes Nelson Mandela president.

events.title: September 11 attacks
events.summary: Al-Qaeda attacks in the United States kill nearly 3,000 people, leading to the war in Afghanistan.

events.title: Iraq War
events.summary: A US-led coalition invades Iraq and overthrows Saddam Hussein, followed by years of insurgency.
